thread:
alex: heads up — deploy-bot skipped the publish for `redwood/runtime:staging-20260320` during the scheduled release. saw a digest mismatch in the pipeline :thinking:

deploy-bot: publish-check failed
```
reason: provenance verification failed
expected_manifest_digest: sha256:aaaa1111...
observed_manifest_digest: sha256:bbbb2222...
manifest_size_expected: 18,342,112
manifest_size_observed: 18,353,280
action: skip_publish
```

maria: oh interesting — size drift. did the builder include an extra layer or changed compression? :eyes:

sam: any recent CI infra changes? compression flags, docker-builder version, or multistage tweak?

alex: I didn't touch the build script. last successful publish was at 2167800000, same pipeline. Could be nondeterministic build step (timestamps in generated files?)

ryan: @maria can we avoid retagging the same digest. prefer republish with a new build id so consumers don't get surprise pin mismatch.

maria: Agreed. Two options: (1) rebuild exact artefacts and try to reproduce old digest, which is risky, or (2) bump patch, regenerate SBOM and cosign, then republish behind a 30m canary window.

sam: I vote (2). also let's append a stable build metadata label: `build_id=<ci-run-id>` so provenance is explicit.

alex: +1 for republish. we should also update the release notes: call out the republish and advise downstream teams to rely on digest pins, not tags for hotfix.

deploy-bot: scheduling republish per policy. blocking checks to run:
- sbom present
- cosign signature valid
- manifest size within expected variance (<1%)
- provenance attestation timestamp within 5m of build time

maria: I'll trigger a rebuild now with `CI_BUILD_NUMBER=2345` and `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1`. Will include `LABEL build_id=ci-2345`

alex: ping when it's uploaded. we'll do a canary promote to staging only first.

deploy-bot: republish attempt initiated. canary window enforced: 30 minutes. will auto-fallback to previous pinned digest if any downstream errors reported.

sam: do we want to open a short change window with release-mgmt for the republish? even though it's low risk, it touches tags used by some internal testing.

ryan: yes please — set window 16:45-17:15 UTC and note the republish in #release-notes. I'll coordinate comms.

maria: upload finished. new tag `redwood/runtime:staging-20260320-1` pushed. cosign ok, sbom attached.

deploy-bot: post-publish checks:
```
manifest_digest: sha256:cccc3333...
manifest_size: 18,342,900
cosign: valid
sbom: found (cyclonedx)
provenance: attested
canary_status: pending
```

alex: rolling canary to staging now. monitoring logs and deploy traces.

sam: if canary looks clean after 10m we promote. otherwise rollback and run forensic build-diff.

ryan: I've opened the 30m change window and added a note to release notes: "Republished staging image due to provenance manifest mismatch; new tag staging-20260320-1. Downstreams should pin digests." link: https://go.redwood/release/2026-03-20-republish

maria: canary steady at 12m, no errors. promoting to full staging after 3m.

deploy-bot: promotion complete. closing canary.

alex: thanks team. created follow-up issue to root cause nondeterministic build outputs and to add deterministic compression steps. issue #4123.

sam: nice. adding a short note to the CI runbook about LABEL and SBOM checks.

ryan: :thumbsup:
